Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Maintain client confidentiality and ethical standards
Situation2: An internal assistant unfamiliar with the matter requests access to sensitive client files for convenience.
Story: It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me awake. My best friend’s name flashed on the screen, and I answered to the sound of her sobs. She could barely speak, her words tumbling out about her father’s sudden illness. I listened, heart aching, offering comfort and promising to stay on the line as long as she needed. In the background, my work phone chimed with an urgent message from the office. An assistant, new to our team, was requesting access to confidential client files, insisting it was necessary to meet a looming deadline. My mind raced—my friend needed me to be present, to listen, to care. But as a lawyer, I was bound by strict rules; I couldn’t just hand over sensitive information, no matter the pressure. I felt torn, my loyalty to my friend pulling me one way, my professional duty tugging me another. The weight of both expectations pressed down on me, and I sat in the dark, phone in hand, caught between two worlds, unsure which to answer first.
